Reignition of the Verdant Years Chapter 18: The Certificate to Take Home

A graduation dinner that began at just past five in the afternoon didn't end until eight at night.

Although they weren't drinking alcohol, the sorrow brought on by the parting was more intoxicating than any liquor.

After night fell, everyone said their goodbyes at the entrance of Jiangnan Restaurant.

Two more sentimental female students, who lived in the city and likely wouldn't be attending high school in Yinjiang District, clung to their best friends and cried their eyes out.

For those who lived far away, parents had already arrived by car to pick up their children.

Li Luo and the others lived near the school, so after bidding Teacher Zhang farewell, they walked away along the sidewalk with Ying Chanxi and the others.

"Burp~" Walking down the road, Li Luo rubbed his slightly bloated belly. "I feel like half of my stomach is filled with juice."

During the first half of the meal, everyone on the table had gone to toast the teachers.

Once things loosened up in the second half, the little brats all started acting like adults, toasting each other and pouring their hearts out, claiming that not drinking meant you looked down on your buddies.

They were really bringing the dregs of the culture to the dinner table.

It was as if only by doing so could they show how much they had grown.

In the midst of this, right before the dinner ended, three boys had even run up to Ying Chanxi to confess.

One was from their own Class Five, and the other two were from the neighboring Class Six. Usually, they kept to themselves, but now that graduation was here and they were about to part for good, they finally mustered up the courage, deciding to put this love to the flame and let it burn completely.

Why put it like that? Because no one went into it expecting Ying Chanxi to agree.

Rather than a confession, it was more like giving a final account for the palpitations of their three years of junior high.

Including the boys who didn't confess, who hadn't had some fantasies about a "white moonlight" like Ying Chanxi?

But Ying Chanxi's polite smiles of thanks and gentle rejections still sent such fantasies to their graves in the beautiful years of youth.

The remaining boys looked on with envious eyes, watching that scoundrel Li Luo help Ying Chanxi sling her schoolbag over her shoulder with complete naturalness.

Many people in the class knew that the two were childhood friends who lived right across the hall from each other.

However, the two of them had never indicated anything, remaining just like the good friends they had been since childhood.

Even so, being able to be by Ying Chanxi's side every day and listen to her talk was something enviable enough for many people.

Li Luo, who was in paradise but didn't know it, let out a burp, unzipped Ying Chanxi's schoolbag, checked his own certificate, and only let out a sigh of relief after confirming it wasn't damaged or creased.

"Do you have to be so careful?" Seeing his pathetic look, Ying Chanxi at his side couldn't help but laugh. "This kind of award doesn't really have any practical meaning. It just sounds nice."

Unlike an "Excellent Teacher" title, which could serve as a foundation for competing for a professional teaching title, the "Outstanding Graduate" award from Yucai Middle School was purely an award, with no practical benefits.

At most, when they got to high school, they could use it to bluff the head teacher and classmates at the beginning of the term to compete for a position as a class officer.

But Li Luo raised his eyebrows and said to Ying Chanxi in a righteous tone, "You, a certificate wholesaler, naturally don't understand the pain of a slacker like me."

"I've been studying for over ten years, and this is the first time I've gotten such a prestigious award."

"I have to frame this directly on the living room wall, so my parents can admire it every day."

Ying Chanxi smiled, pursing her lips, then asked, "Then can my certificate be hung on your wall too?"

"Why would your certificate be hung at my place?" Li Luo said with a speechless expression. "Do you have to show off in front of me?"

"No," Ying Chanxi said, blinking. "I have too many certificates, and there's no space to hang them at home. I want to borrow your wall."

"...Ying Chanxi, don't try to flex so awkwardly in the future. It's a bit annoying."

"Then I won't ask you. I'll go back and ask Uncle and Auntie."

"Then I'm begging you. At least wait until I take my certificate out and show it to my parents first."

"Since you've begged me like this, I suppose I have no choice but to reluctantly agree."

The two of them bickered and chatted casually all the way, and soon enough, the other classmates who were walking the same way had all disappeared.

By the time they came back to their senses, there was no one else around them, just the two of them walking side-by-side toward home.

...

At 8:30 PM, Jincheng Residential Community.

Li Guohong was leaning back on the sofa with a cigarette in his mouth, quietly enjoying the feeling of the white smoke curling upwards.

On the other side, Lin Xiuhong was on the phone with a wide smile on her face.

"Yes, that's right! 555 points!"

"Oh, isn't that just it? Fu Yi Zhong is a sure thing now."

"Not at all, not at all, it's not that exaggerated. It's all because the boy worked hard himself."

"Yes, of course, we have to celebrate. Isn't that why I'm calling you?"

"It's next weekend. Are you two free?"

"Great, great, then it's a deal."

From the time she got home after closing the breakfast shop in the evening until now, Lin Xiuhong had already made over ten phone calls.

By now, basically all the relatively close relatives knew that Xiuhong's son, Li Luo, had scored 555 on the high school entrance exam this year and was guaranteed to get into Fu Yi Zhong.

At the same time, it was already decided that they would hold a school-advancement banquet for Li Luo next weekend to celebrate his successful admission to Fu Yi Zhong.

Originally, Li Guohong had wanted to help with the calls.

But Lin Xiuhong pushed him away, insisting on making them all by herself.

She was on the phone for a full two hours before she finished calling all the relatively close relatives.

After talking non-stop for two hours, a normal person's mouth and throat would have long gone dry.

But Lin Xiuhong felt completely refreshed at this moment. It had been a long time since she had felt so invigorated and clear-headed, as if her very soul had been sublimated.

"In total, it should be about three tables," Lin Xiuhong said to Li Guohong after putting down her phone. "That restaurant of Shufen's family isn't booked for next weekend. Why don't we go ahead and book three tables? Since we know them, we can get a bit of a discount."

"Alright, let's book it then," Li Guohong nodded. "Little Uncle's family is coming too, right?"

"They're coming," Lin Xiuhong said. "Don't we need to talk to them about the house? It's a good chance to invite them for a meal and discuss it in detail at the dinner table."

"Mmm," Li Guohong thought for a moment, nodded slightly, and then said, "Then about Wei Dongrong..."

"Let's put that on hold for now?" Lin Xiuhong thought about it. "After all, the matter with Little Uncle's house isn't completely settled yet. How about we turn Wei Dongrong down after we're sure we can buy it?"

"That makes sense," Li Guohong agreed with his wife's idea, then couldn't help but sigh with emotion. "It really feels like a dream. How on earth did that kid, Li Luo, score so well?"

As he said this, Li Guohong felt Lin Xiuhong lean in closer to him.

The next second, a hand gently slapped him across the face.

"Wait... what are you doing?" Li Guohong covered one side of his face and looked at his wife in astonishment.

"Didn't you say it feels like a dream?" Lin Xiuhong chuckled. "Does it hurt? If it hurts, it's not a dream."

"I really have you to thank for that."

As the old couple chatted idly at home, the sound of a key in the lock came from the front door.

The next second, Li Luo opened the door and walked in.

Ying Chanxi followed behind him.

"Dad, Mom, your pride and joy has returned!" Li Luo walked into the house, changed into his slippers, then strode into the living room with a triumphant look on his face, spreading his arms and announcing loudly, "Did you miss me?"

Perhaps it was the effect of teenage hormones, but Li Luo was getting more and more used to his 15-year-old identity.

But Li Guohong and Lin Xiuhong just looked at their son's behavior and said to Ying Chanxi behind him, "Xixi, come and sit."

Ying Chanxi obediently sat down next to Lin Xiuhong. She glanced at Li Luo, and after seeing his gesturing gaze, she had no choice but to open her schoolbag, pick out a certificate, and hand it to her uncle and auntie.

"Auntie Lin, look, what's this?"

"Hm?" Lin Xiuhong was taken aback for a moment as she took the certificate from Ying Chanxi's hand.

Li Guohong also leaned over, reading aloud as he looked, "Congratulations to student Li Luo for winning the... 2014... Outstanding Graduate title from Yucai Middle School?"

"What kind of award is this?" Lin Xiuhong asked strangely. "Did the school give it to him? Or did he buy it himself from the corner store?"

"Wait... Mom, that kind of doubt is really heartbreaking," Li Luo said, unconvinced. "Of course, the school gave it to me! I even went on stage to receive the award at the graduation ceremony today! I'll ask Teacher Zhang for the group photo from the award ceremony another day."

"Of course I'm willing to believe you," Lin Xiuhong glanced at her son. "But for an award that even you can get, our Xixi must have one too. Otherwise, even if it's real, this certificate doesn't have much value."

Li Luo: "..."

Seeing Li Luo's speechless expression, Ying Chanxi, who was sitting next to Lin Xiuhong, immediately covered her mouth to stifle a laugh, her shoulders trembling with mirth.

Finally, having no other choice, Ying Chanxi had to pull her own certificate out of her schoolbag as well.

"Auntie Lin, I actually received one too," Ying Chanxi kindly explained for Li Luo. "Only 11 students in the entire school could get this Outstanding Graduate award. Li Luo is already amazing."

"Oh, for real now," Lin Xiuhong took Ying Chanxi's certificate, examined it carefully, and then immediately said, "Then I'll have to put both of your certificates up together."

"Wouldn't just posting mine be enough?" Li Luo grumbled. "It's a rare occasion for me."

"It's precisely because it's rare that we have to post Xixi's too!" Lin Xiuhong said, analyzing it for him with a straight face. "Only with Xixi's certificate posted next to it will yours have enough value. Otherwise, who would know what kind of bogus award it is?"

Son of a...

Li Luo's face contorted as if he had a toothache.

Ying Chanxi, on the other hand, laughed even more happily, clinging to Lin Xiuhong's arm and shaking with laughter, unable to stop.

However, Ying Chanxi was still considerate of Li Luo. She took out the photocopy of the full-score essay from her bag and handed it to her uncle and auntie.

"Auntie Lin, look at this," Ying Chanxi patiently introduced. "Li Luo got a perfect score on his language arts essay this time. This is it. It's really well-written. I only got a perfect score a few times in all three years of junior high."

"Whoa!" Li Guohong was instantly surprised upon hearing this. "He got a perfect score on his essay too? Then I'll have to take a good look at this."

Lin Xiuhong and Li Guohong began to read it seriously, sometimes even reading it aloud, which made Li Luo feel a wave of second-hand embarrassment.

But seeing how happy his parents looked, Li Luo felt an awkward yet satisfying pleasure, a great sense of fulfillment in his heart.

However, the couple's education level was not high, and their appreciation skills were limited, so afterward, they could only say that it was well-written.

By the time they finished talking about all this, it was already past nine o'clock.

Ying Chanxi said her goodbyes and went home. After walking her next door, Li Luo went across the hall to use their computer for a bit, pinging his editor Qianzhou on QQ to see if he was online.

The work-drone editor was still online even at this hour, so Li Luo returned home. After finding that his dad had already showered and gone to his bedroom to rest, he pulled his mom, who was about to go shower, to sit down on the sofa.

"Mom, do you know why I wrote my essay so well?"

"Why?" Lin Xiuhong asked with a look of curious confusion. "Do you have some kind of trick for that?"

"Of course I do," Li Luo nodded repeatedly, then his expression turned serious as he said, "Actually, it's like this. I'll tell you a secret..."
